product: commentary — no product (competitor teardown of Resilia oil of oregano)
hook: "Resilia is one of the fastest scaling supplement brands on Meta right now… they're pushing toward $1M a day in spend, testing something like 6,000 ads."
body: A full strategic teardown of Resilia's parasite angle: a cause-RELOCATION play — the viewer blames diet/age/stress, the ad relocates blame to parasites hiding behind gut biofilm, then gates the solution (store oregano oil is 30-50% carvacrol, "too weak"; Resilia's wild Mediterranean oregano is 85%, "the only combo strong enough," plus black seed oil to flush the dead). The signature script beat: list symptoms (jaw clenching, crawling skin at night, 2-3am wakeups, belly pooch, shoulder pain) and after each — "That's parasites." None of the claims live on the product page; 10+ subpages dodge bans. The stealable structure: find where the customer assigns blame → relocate the cause to something invisible → gate the solution with a mechanism only your product passes.
cta: DM "Audit" for a creative audit (author's agency CTA); link to the top landing page.
idea: One properly constructed angle (cause relocation + mechanism gate) feeds an entire account for months — every symptom becomes a re-skin, not a reinvention.
sequencing: Scale proof: ~$1M/day spend, 6,000 ads, one angle.
THE RELOCATION: blame diet/age/stress → parasites behind biofilm.
The roll-call beat: symptom list, each answered "That's parasites."
THE BIOFILM: pre-kill the doctor objection ("they'd rather you keep coming back").
The gate: 30-50% carvacrol too weak; 85% is the only combo strong enough.
THE FUNNEL SPLIT: claims live on subpages/advertorials, never the PDP.
WHAT TO STEAL: the 3-step structure (find blame → relocate → gate).
Volume thesis: angle first, volume downstream.
formatting: Long article-style teardown with section headers (THE RELOCATION / THE BIOFILM / THE FUNNEL SPLIT / WHAT TO STEAL).
why_it_works: Cause relocation gives the viewer a villain (not themselves) and the brand a monopoly on the solution — the gate turns a commodity into the only qualifying answer.
what_to_steal: The 3-step relocation structure is LC's sharpest weapon: customers blame themselves/"cheap jewelry" for green skin and tarnish → relocate to the invisible culprit (flash plating, nickel, thin gold wash) → gate with the mechanism only LC passes (14K PVD over 316L steel, lifetime color warranty). One angle, endless re-skins.

hook: "BlackRock is buying Shapoorji bonds. Retail platforms are already using this as a marketing hook."
body: A two-line finance thread opener: BlackRock is buying Shapoorji bonds, retail platforms are using it as a marketing hook — "Before you buy 'the bond BlackRock bought' read this." The buyer's-guide warning pattern applied to bond marketing.
idea: The authority-hijack warning: before you buy what the big name bought, read the fine print — the buyer's-guide flip as financial content.
sequencing: News: BlackRock buying Shapoorji bonds.
Observation: retail platforms already using it as a hook.
Warning: "Before you buy 'the bond BlackRock bought' read this."
Pattern: the authority-hijack warning as the buyer's-guide flip.
why_it_works: Borrowing BlackRock's authority to create the warning makes the caution feel like insider protection rather than a sales pitch.
what_to_steal: The "before you buy the [authority-endorsed] X" headline template for LC: "Before you buy the 'waterproof' jewelry the influencers wear, read this" — then flip the label on what waterproof actually means.

product: commentary — no product (teardown of "Thriving Through Midlife" ad)
hook: "spring sale | up to 63% off . today only"
body: A mini-teardown of a "Thriving Through Midlife" ad: hook "spring sale | up to 63% off — today only," specificity play ("sounds too good to be true? try it before you buy it"), 60-day trial / money-back guarantee, limited-time offer. 143s video + photo; the post is a "worth breaking down" analyst note.
cta: The ad's CTA (per the teardown): limited-time offer link.
idea: The analyst's lens: a midlife brand's ad dissected into hook + specificity + risk reversal — the warning-flip is in the teardown format itself.
sequencing: Brand + hook: Thriving Through Midlife, "spring sale | up to 63% off, today only."
Specificity: "sounds too good to be true? try it before you buy it."
Risk reversal: 60 days or money back, guaranteed.
Scarcity: limited-time offer link.
formatting: Short analyst note + 143s video + photo. "Worth breaking this one down" framing.
why_it_works: Naming the beats turns one ad into a reusable diagnostic other operators can run on their own creatives.
what_to_steal: The 4-beat offer autopsy (hook → specificity → risk reversal → scarcity) as LC's checklist for auditing its own promo ads — every sale creative should pass all four.

body: A thread teaser: Resilia is "PRINTING $36M/month" (unverified) with AI-generated ads; the edge isn't creation (Higgsfield made that cheap) but "HOW you structure and position the messaging." Promises a breakdown of their top 5 ads: candida, aged garlic 4-week arteries, GLP-1, urgency (8 at once), animated explainer.
idea: When AI makes creation free, the only edge left is message structure and positioning — Resilia's top 5 as the proof set.
sequencing: Claim: $36M/month with AI ads.
Thesis: creation is commoditized; structure is the edge.
Tease: top-5 breakdown (candida, aged garlic, GLP-1, urgency ×8, animated explainer).
Thread promise.
why_it_works: "$36M/month" + a contrarian thesis (the tool isn't the edge) creates a curiosity gap the thread promises to close.
what_to_steal: The strategic reframe for LC's AI program: stop competing on generation quality (everyone has the models) and compete on message architecture — the angle, the gate, the sequencing.

product: Directory ad spots (nicklaunches' own ad product)
hook: "Before you buy ANY directory ad, ask these 4."
body: A buyer's-guide warning deployed as direct response for the author's own product: "Before you buy ANY directory ad, ask these 4" — who measures the traffic (them or third party), how many ads rotate through the spot, is it on 1 page or every page, can you cancel any month. Then his answers: Cloudflare-measured, 246K visitors in 9 days, 4 spots, (link). The warning IS the pitch.
cta: The link to his directory ad spots (4 spots, Cloudflare-verified traffic).
idea: The buyer's-guide flip as a sales letter: teach the 4 questions that disqualify competitors, then answer them yourself.
sequencing: Warning headline: before you buy ANY directory ad, ask these 4.
Q1: who measures the traffic — them or a third party.
Q2: how many ads rotate through the same spot.
Q3: is it on 1 page or every page.
Q4: can you cancel any month.
The flip: his answers (Cloudflare, 246K visitors/9 days, 4 spots).
CTA: the link.
formatting: Short text post + photo. Blockquote checklist style.
why_it_works: Teaching the buyer to interrogate the category positions the author as the honest broker, and the 4 questions are engineered so only his product passes all of them.
what_to_steal: The exact flip for LC: "Before you buy ANY 'waterproof' jewelry, ask these 4" (is it PVD or flash-plated? 316L steel or mystery alloy? what's the warranty in writing? does it survive the pool test?) — then answer with LC's specs. The warning sells the label check.
